The patella is laterally subluxed and there is diffuse edema seen along the course of the medial patellofemoral ligament consistent with a high-grade injury. This extends to the femoral attachment and also involves the attachment at the patella. The lateral patellar retinaculum is intact and appears unremarkable.

There is intraosseous edema within the medial patella and contour flattening of the medial surface of the patella. There is associated edema in the lateral femoral condyle consistent associated with the osteochondral impaction along the lateral cortical surface in keeping with transient lateral dislocation of the patella associated with osteochondral impaction of the medial surface of the patella and lateral femoral condyle.

The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

There is trochlea dysplasia and lateralization of the tibial tubercle with the TT-TG distance measuring 2.1 cm. Articular cartilage of the patella demonstrates focal fraying at the patellar apex. The trochlear surface is reasonably well-maintained.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment appears to be well maintained.

The medial meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is well-maintained.

The anterior cruciate ligament is intact and appears unremarkable.

There is mild intrinsic signal within the posterior cruciate ligament but intact fibers are present and the signal changes may in part be artifactual.

There is edema around the proximal and mid fibers of the medial collateral ligament consistent with low-grade medial collateral ligament sprain.

The lateral collateral ligament complex including fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon, popliteus tendon and IT band all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is a small to moderate knee effusion. There is no Baker's cyst demonstrated.

INTERPRETATION: 

Torn medial patellofemoral ligament associated with bone contusions an osteochondral fracturing of the medial surface of patella and lateral femoral condyle associated with transient dislocation of the patellofemoral joint.

Moderate chondromalacia patella.

Background changes of lateralization of the tibial tubercle and shallowness of the trochlear groove predisposing to patellar dislocation.

Low-grade medial collateral ligament tear.

Nonspecific signal in the posterior cruciate ligament favored to be artifactual.
